title: The ham that never weighs 500 g
question: How is probability shared out over possible results?
hook: A scale with endless precision will never read exactly 500 g, yet a pack can still pass inspection.
idea: A distribution shares probability across outcomes: discrete ones give each value a probability, while continuous ones give probability to ranges.

beats.prompt: A scale can show arbitrarily many digits. What is the probability that a piece of ham weighs exactly 500 g?

choices.label: Small but above zero
choices.feedback: It tempts because some packs surely land near 500 g, but however many digits you read, further non-zero digits could follow.

choices.label: One half
choices.feedback: Exactly 500 g is one value among endlessly many, so it cannot be this likely.

choices.label: It depends on the scale
choices.feedback: More precision does not rescue it: it stays zero at any chosen level of precision.

beats.explain: Whatever precision you pick, you cannot rule out non-zero digits beyond it, so an exact value has probability zero.

beats.prompt: Sort each situation by the kind of distribution that describes it.
items: The temperature on a given day
A weight read to arbitrarily many digits
beats.explain: Coin tosses and die rolls have a discrete set of outcomes; temperature and exact weight take values in a continuous range.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it does.
pairs: Gives the probability of being no larger than a value
Gives probabilities for a single random variable
beats.explain: Each is a way of describing a distribution, chosen by the kind of variable and the question asked.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A scale shows a ham's weight to as many digits as you like.
Further non-zero digits could always follow, so exactly 500 g has probability zero.
But a pack must weigh between 490 g and 510 g to pass inspection.
So passing inspection must also have probability zero.
beats.explain: A range covers infinitely many outcomes and needs no infinite precision, so it can have positive probability.
